documents.t: NalamDesk is a secure, offline-first clinic management system. Your patient data lives on your own computer, encrypted, and the clinic runs its full day with no internet. Start with the User Guide: Initial Setup: create the encrypted vault and the administrator account. Admin Management: clinic details, staff accounts, backups. Clinic Operations: registration, queue and triage, consultations, prescriptions. Daily Collection: receipts and the ledger-derived day close. Merging Duplicate Charts: preview-first merge with rollback. NalamDesk is free software under AGPL-3.0. The code lives on GitHub and installers ship from GitHub Releases.
NalamDesk takes data security seriously. We employ a Privacy-First, Local-First architecture. This means your patient data resides on your device, encrypted, and is never sent to our servers.

NalamDesk automatically creates an encrypted backup of your database every day at the time configured under Settings > Data & Backup > Local Backup Schedule (default 1:00 PM). The app must be open at that time for the backup to run. Backup schedule, health, location, restore, and Drive sync live under Settings, Data and Backup.

Unless you configure a custom location, backups are stored in the application data folder: Windows: C:\Users\<YourUser>\AppData\Roaming\NalamDesk\backups macOS: /Users/<YourUser>/Library/Application Support/NalamDesk/backups Linux: /home/<YourUser>/.config/nalamdesk/backups
Local backups are retained for 30 days. Older backups are automatically deleted to save space.
Go to Settings > Data & Backup. Click Change Location under the Local Backups section. Select your preferred folder (e.g., an external hard drive or a specific document folder for easier access).

The Data & Backup screen reports backup health derived from the backup files on disk: when the last backup ran and whether anything needs attention. A Run backup now action is offered when a problem is found.

Go to Settings > Data & Backup > Restore from Backup File (the same picker is available on the Welcome screen before login). Click Choose Backup File… and pick a .ndbackup file. Enter the Recovery Code and the current administrator password. Both are required. There is no reset path: a lost recovery code means the backup cannot be restored. Click Restore Vault. The app restarts with the restored data.

For off-site redundancy, you can sync your backups to your personal Google Drive. NalamDesk uses a Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) model, giving you full control over the connection and ensuring we cannot access your Drive.

Step 1: Create a Google Cloud Project​ Go to Google Cloud Console. Click Select a Project > New Project. Name it NalamDesk Backup and click Create. Step 2: Enable Google Drive API​ On the left sidebar, go to APIs & Services > Library. Search for Google Drive API and click Enable. Step 3: Configure OAuth Consent Screen​ Go to APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen. Select External (for personal use) and click Create. Fill in required fields: App Name: NalamDesk Backup User Support Email: Your email Developer Contact Info: Your email Click Save and Continue. Scopes: Add .../auth/drive.file. Test Users: Add your own Gmail address. Step 4: Create Credentials​ Go to APIs & Services > Credentials. Click Create Credentials > OAuth client ID. Application Type: Select Desktop app. Name: NalamDesk Desktop Client. Click Create. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret. Step 5: Connect NalamDesk​ Open NalamDesk > Settings > Data & Backup. Paste your Client ID and Client Secret. Click Connect Drive and approve the permissions in the browser window. Once connected, NalamDesk will upload the daily encrypted backup to a hidden appDataFolder in your Google Drive, ensuring it doesn't clutter your main Drive view.
NalamDesk uses a secure, local-first hybrid desktop architecture designed for resilience and performance.

Component Technology Description Runtime Electron Cross-platform desktop environment. Frontend Angular + TailwindCSS Responsive, component-based UI. Backend Fastify High-performance local Node.js server. Database SQLite + SQLCipher Encrypted local data storage. Security Argon2 Industry-standard password hashing.

Entry Point: src/main/main.ts Responsibilities: App Window Management. Native System Integrations (File System, Dialogs). Auto-updates (electron-updater) against a generic HTTPS clinic feed (NALAMDESK_UPDATE_FEED_URL) in packaged builds; GitHub provider is a later-PR seam (NALAMDESK_UPDATE_PROVIDER=github). Linux gnome-libsecret password-store switch at process start. Authenticated desktop session (SessionService); auth:logout clears the principal.

Entry Point: src/server/app.ts (bootstrapped via src/server/bootstrap.ts, served by src/server/index.ts; built with tsconfig.server.json) Port: 3000 (Localhost) Role: Validates requests and proxies them to the DatabaseService. Security: JWT Authentication: Validates tokens on protected routes. IP Restriction: With STRICT_ADMIN_IP=true, admin login is restricted to local IP (127.0.0.1 or ::1) to prevent network-based attacks. The server otherwise listens on all interfaces (0.0.0.0:3000); the header shows the LAN URL for clinic devices. Renderer access: the Angular app reaches the main process through a preload IPC bridge (src/main/preload.ts); the local API additionally serves LAN consumers with token + RBAC checks.

Service: src/main/services/DatabaseService.ts Engine: better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers Encryption: The entire database file (nalamdesk.db) is encrypted on disk. The encryption key is derived securely, ensuring that data is inaccessible without proper authentication.

graph TD User[User] -->|Interact| UI[Angular Frontend] UI -->|HTTP POST (JWT)| Server[Fastify Server (Port 3000)] Server -->|Validate Token & RBAC| Auth[Auth Middleware] Auth -->|Approved| DBService[Database Service] DBService -->|SQL Query| SQLite[(Encrypted SQLite DB)] SQLite -->|Result| DBService DBService -->|JSON Response| UI

NalamDesk uses Argon2, a memory-hard password hashing algorithm, to store user passwords. This makes brute-force attacks computationally expensive and infeasible. Implementation: src/main/services/DatabaseService.ts -> saveUser / validateUser.

Access control is enforced at the API layer, with a shared permission model in src/shared/access.ts (built-in roles admin, doctor, nurse, receptionist; Cedar policy checks behind handler-gated clinical actions) and a permission-conformance spec at src/server/access-conformance.spec.ts. Role Permissions Admin Full Access. User management, custom roles and per-user overrides, Clinic Settings, Backup/Restore. Acts as scribe in consults (must pick the responsible doctor). Doctor Responsible licensed practitioner. Clinical Encounters, Prescriptions, Queue Triage, Vitals, Chart Merge, Billing. Receptionist Patient Registration, Queue Management & Triage, Vitals, Billing & Day Close, Chart Archive. No safety-data edits, no merges. Nurse Patient Vitals, Queue Triage & Monitoring. No queue removal, no billing, no merges. Settings routes additionally require admin (adminGuard redirects everyone else to the dashboard). Handler-gated actions (consult finalization, merges) reject non-qualifying roles even when a custom role or override would otherwise permit them.

To ensure medico-legal compliance and patient safety: Licensed Practitioner Assertion: Every clinical encounter and prescription requires a responsible licensed practitioner with role doctor. Non-practitioner accounts (administrators, receptionists) cannot independently finalize prescriptions or complete encounters without associating a licensed doctor. License Snapshotting: When an encounter is completed, the responsible practitioner's license number is durably snapshotted onto visits.practitioner_license_snapshot, freezing the practitioner's credentials as they existed at the moment of signing. Authorship vs. Attending Doctor: Scribe and assistant entries distinguish the acting user (author_id) from the attending responsible practitioner (doctor_id).

Longitudinal Records: NalamDesk tracks patient allergies/intolerances, active problems (conditions), and active medications across all past encounters. Automated Prescription Medication Sync: Upon completion of a consultation, prescribed medications are automatically reflected in the patient's active medication list. Prescribing Allergy Conflict Detection: Real-time cross-checks compare newly prescribed drugs against documented active allergies. If a conflict is detected, the practitioner is alerted and must provide an explicit clinical override reason (e.g. "Desensitized, patient tolerated previously") before the prescription can be saved.

4-Tier Urgency Hierarchy: Patient flow supports 4 standard urgency tiers (immediate [Priority 4], urgent [Priority 3], priority [Priority 2], routine [Priority 1]). Triage Audit Trail: Every priority reassessment records a historical audit entry in queue_triage_history with the previous priority, new priority, clinical reason, and staff ID. Abnormal Vitals Detection: Vitals observations are automatically evaluated against clinical thresholds; abnormal vitals trigger warning badges in the patient queue to facilitate rapid clinical intervention. Standardized Dual-Unit Vitals Engine: The vitals engine accepts measurements in clinical units (°F or °C, kg or lbs), persists canonical values, and aligns with standard LOINC codes and UCUM unit symbols.

documents.t: How clinical catalog content (medicines, conditions, codes) enters NalamDesk, and the license rules that keep an AGPL app distributed worldwide compliant.

Source What we take License How NLEM 2022 (MoHFW) 384 generic names Free govt PDF; names are facts desktop/scripts/extract_nlem.py → nlem2022.seeds.ts WHO EML 2025 (24th list) Cross-check generics CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO Manual reference ICD-10 (common OP codes) ~58 short codes WHO license required for software distribution Filed/pending; see below ICD-11 MMS 58 mapped codes + URIs CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO (free incl. commercial) desktop/scripts/map_icd11.py (annual) SNOMED CT Nothing vendored Affiliate License mandatory (free in India via NRCeS) Live BHTS queries only Indian brand names Hand-curated examples No official feed exists Curated in migration seeds NLEM 2022 is the latest notified list (CDSCO lists only 2022 and 2015). A revision is publicly demanded but not published as of Oct 2026.

No licensed bulk content in the repo. No SNOMED release files, no WHO ICD CSV dumps. Ever. Codes ship with URIs + citation. CC BY-ND requires ICD-11 codes to travel with their URIs and WHO attribution. Never store a bare code. Facts only in seeds. Short generic names and common code mappings are factual entries, each carrying its source citation. NULL means unmapped. snomed_* and unmapped icd11_* columns stay NULL rather than carrying guessed codes. Wrong medical codes are worse than missing ones. Never hand-write medical codes. All code mappings come from the scripts below, reviewed as data PRs.

The key is a free access credential (rate limiting), not a purchase. It is needed only for the annual mapping run -- never at clinic runtime. Local runs: WHO_ICD_CLIENT_ID / WHO_ICD_CLIENT_SECRET in .env (gitignored). The script reads env only. CI: GitHub repo secret, consumed solely by the manually-dispatched seed-refresh workflow -- never per-PR builds. Never in source, the Electron bundle, the database, logs, or audit trails. Rotate immediately if exposed (free, same portal). Get a key: register at https://icd.who.int/icdapi (free, ~2 minutes).

Every external source and portal in one place: NLEM 2022 PDF (MoHFW via WHO mirror): https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/essential-medicines/national-essential-medicines-lists-(neml)/searo_neml/india-2022.pdf NLEM list page (CDSCO): https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/opencms/en/consumer/Essential-Medicines/ WHO ICD API portal (free key registration): https://icd.who.int/icdapi ICD-11 license: https://icd.who.int/docs/icd-api/license/ ICD-11 offline deployment (Docker / Windows / Linux): https://icd.who.int/docs/icd-api/ICDAPI-LocalDeployment/ SNOMED India licensing (MLDS): https://mlds.ihtsdotools.org/ → landing /IN NRCeS (standards, tools, help nrc-help@cdac.in): https://nrces.in BHTS terminology browser: https://nrces.in/bhts/ BHTS FHIR API base: https://nrces.in/bhts/api/v1/ts/fhir ABDM FHIR profiles (NRCeS): https://nrces.in/ndhm/fhir/r4/ WHO eEML database: https://list.essentialmeds.org/

Run map_icd11.py conditions.txt with the current ICD release. Diff the output; review every changed code as a data change. Paste curated mappings into SEED_CONDITIONS; the migration's stamp-pattern (UPDATE ... WHERE icd11_code IS NULL) applies them. Record the release (e.g. 2025-01) in the seed header comment. Re-run extract_nlem.py only when MoHFW notifies a new NLEM. Seeds are the offline core for version-stamped releases; anything beyond them resolves live when connected (see BHTS below).

Affiliate License (mandatory even though free in India): register at mlds.ihtsdotools.org → landing /IN, activate the account, accept the agreement, request access; download link in 4-5 business days. Help: nrc-help@cdac.in, nrces.in. Scope: an NRCeS license covers use within India. Distribution or use abroad needs per-country licenses -- incompatible with blind global AGPL distribution, so SNOMED features stay gated/BYO-license outside India. BHTS public API (nrces.in/bhts/api/v1/ts/fhir): keyless Snowstorm FHIR -- $lookup, $translate (SNOMED→ICD-10), $expand all verified working. Fine for live queries; confirm terms before production-scale traffic, and never persist answers into shipped seeds (that is redistribution).

ICD-11 first: free license, PM-JAY precedent (live in all states since Apr 2022), offline container available. ICD-10 seeds retained per issue #56 and EHR Standards 2016. SNOMED deferred: no current use case (drug/allergy/procedure coding); columns reserved, BHTS covers live lookup. Brands curated: no official brand↔generic feed exists; hand list stays, clearly labeled.

NalamDesk uses a relational SQLite database (SQLCipher-encrypted via better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers). Schema evolves through ordered migrations in desktop/src/main/schema/migrations.ts (currently v39, with a spec asserting each step in migrations.spec.ts). Below is the schema definition for core tables.

Stores credentials and profile information for all system users (Doctors, Staff, Admin). Column Type Description id INTEGER PK Auto-incrementing ID. username TEXT UNIQUE Login username. password TEXT Argon2 Hash of the password. role TEXT admin, doctor, receptionist, nurse. name TEXT Display name. specialty TEXT Doctor's specialty (e.g., General Physician). license_number TEXT Medical license number. active INTEGER 1 for active, 0 for soft-delete. mobile, email TEXT Contact details (mobile is 10 digits in the UI). abdm_hpr_id TEXT Doctor's ABDM Health Professional Registry ID (optional). Custom roles live in roles; per-user permission grants/forbids in user_permission_overrides (Migrations v32–v33 seed the grant tables; v31 adds the overrides table).

Core patient registry. Column Type Description id INTEGER PK Unique Patient ID. uuid TEXT UNIQUE System-generated UUID for syncing. name TEXT Patient Name. mobile TEXT Contact Number. date_of_birth DATE Date of Birth (ISO format YYYY-MM-DD). Age is calculated dynamically. gender TEXT Male, Female, Other (Unknown also accepted in the UI). address TEXT Residential address. mrn TEXT UNIQUE Auto-assigned medical record number (ND-000001 style; prefix configurable via settings.mrn_prefix). Added in Migration v35. dob_estimated INTEGER 1 when age was typed directly instead of picked from a birth date. Added in Migration v35. merged_into INTEGER NULL Points at the surviving chart after a merge; cleared on unmerge. Added in Migration v35. active INTEGER 1 normally, 0 for archived charts. Added in Migration v38. archive_reason TEXT Recorded reason for archiving. Added in Migration v38.

Records clinical encounters. Column Type Description id INTEGER PK Visit ID. patient_id INTEGER FK Links to patients.id. doctor_id INTEGER FK Responsible licensed practitioner (users.id). author_id INTEGER FK Links to users.id (Author/scribe recording encounter). practitioner_license_snapshot TEXT Snapshot of responsible doctor's license at signing. allergy_override_reason TEXT Clinical justification if prescribed medicine conflicts with allergy. date DATETIME Timestamp of the visit. diagnosis TEXT Medical diagnosis notes. prescription_json TEXT JSON string array of medicines. amount_paid NUMERIC(12,2) Consultation fee collected.

Stores structured clinical observations (FHIR Observation aligned) linked durably to patients, encounters, and pre-consultation queues. Supports dual-unit entry (°F/°C, kg/lbs), LOINC and UCUM standardized representation, and non-destructive amendment history. Column Type Description id INTEGER PK Auto-incrementing Observation ID. visit_id INTEGER FK Links to visits.id (Encounter linkage). NULL if recorded pre-consultation. patient_id INTEGER FK Links to patients.id. systolic_bp INTEGER Systolic blood pressure (mmHg, 50–300; LOINC 8480-6). diastolic_bp INTEGER Diastolic blood pressure (mmHg, 30–200; LOINC 8462-4). pulse INTEGER Heart rate (bpm, 30–250; LOINC 8867-4). temperature REAL Body temperature (50–115 °F canonical; LOINC 8310-5). weight REAL Patient weight (0.5–500 kg canonical; LOINC 29463-7). height REAL Patient height (20–300 cm; LOINC 8302-2). bmi REAL Body Mass Index (auto-calculated; LOINC 39156-5). spo2 REAL Oxygen saturation (50–100 %; LOINC 59408-5). respiratory_rate REAL Respiratory rate (4–80 bpm; LOINC 9279-1). created_at DATETIME Timestamp row was created. effective_time DATETIME Clinical observation timestamp. recorded_at DATETIME System entry timestamp. performer_id INTEGER FK Links to users.id (clinician who measured vitals). status TEXT FHIR status: preliminary, final, amended, corrected, entered-in-error. units_json TEXT JSON object specifying display units and UCUM standard codes. queue_entry_id INTEGER FK Links to patient_queue.id for queue-side vitals persistence. replaces_id INTEGER FK Self-reference to previous vitals ID when amended/corrected. amendment_reason TEXT Clinical justification for amendment. client_request_id TEXT Idempotency key to prevent duplicate submissions.

Longitudinal record of patient allergies, adverse reactions, and drug intolerances. Column Type Description id INTEGER PK Allergy record ID. patient_id INTEGER FK Links to patients.id. substance TEXT Allergen name (e.g. Penicillin, Sulfa, Peanuts). verification_status TEXT confirmed, unconfirmed, refuted. criticality TEXT low, high (life-threatening), unable-to-assess. severity TEXT mild, moderate, severe. reaction TEXT Manifestation description (e.g. Anaphylaxis, Urticaria). status TEXT active, inactive, resolved. notes TEXT Free-text clinical notes. recorder_id INTEGER FK Links to users.id (Clinician who logged allergy). recorded_at DATETIME Timestamp when recorded.

Longitudinal problem list and chronic condition registry. Column Type Description id INTEGER PK Condition record ID. patient_id INTEGER FK Links to patients.id. condition_name TEXT Condition / problem description. code TEXT ICD-10 diagnostic code (optional). category TEXT problem-list-item, encounter-diagnosis, chronic-condition. clinical_status TEXT active, recurrence, relapse, inactive, remission, resolved. onset_date DATE Approximate or exact onset date. notes TEXT Clinical notes and severity observations. recorder_id INTEGER FK Links to users.id. recorded_at DATETIME Timestamp when recorded.

Longitudinal active medication list, updated manually or automatically synchronized upon encounter completion. Column Type Description id INTEGER PK Medication record ID. patient_id INTEGER FK Links to patients.id. medicine_name TEXT Brand or generic medicine name. dosage TEXT Dose specification (e.g., 500mg). frequency TEXT Dosage schedule (e.g., 1-0-1 After Food). status TEXT active, completed, stopped, on-hold. start_date DATE Start date of prescription/regimen. end_date DATE Expected or actual completion date. notes TEXT Indication or compliance remarks. recorder_id INTEGER FK Links to users.id. recorded_at DATETIME Timestamp when recorded.
Clinic-local diagnoses for Plan & Rx typeahead. Unique name among active rows. Soft-retire sets active = 0 and does not rewrite historical visit text.
Clinic-local medicines with optional default Rx fields (form, dosage, route, frequency, duration, instruction) matching the visit prescription snapshot.
Ordered default Rx lines for a condition (condition_id, sort_order, optional medicine_id, plus snapshot columns matching PrescriptionItem). Applied into the editable Rx list on diagnosis pick.

One chart can carry several identifiers at once: clinic MRN, ABHA number / address, insurance, and free-form ids. patients.mrn and abha_address stay as fast-path columns; patient_identifiers is the extensible registry (system, type_code, value, is_primary), unique per (system, value). patients.abha_number holds the nationally-unique ABHA number (unique where present). Registry reads and writes are granted to doctors, receptionists, and admins.

Immutable money trail: invoices with charge lines, payments as append-only rows, corrections through reversals — never edits. invoices: unique number, visit_id, patient_id, total (computed from lines), status, plus discount/tax. Created only for finished visits; the clinic consultation_fee setting prepends the first line when non-zero. invoice_items: one row per charge line (description, quantity, rate, amount). payments: unique receipt_no, invoice_id, kind (payment or reversal), amount, method (cash, upi, card), reference, reason, idempotency key. Refunds insert reversal rows; voids cancel invoices with a reason and are blocked while payments are outstanding. The day-close report (getDailyClose) derives collected totals, by-method breakdowns, and the review queue purely from these rows.

patient_merges: one row per merge (survivor_id, duplicate_id, audited reason), reversible via unmerge. patient_merge_items: every moved row (table, id column, row id) so unmerge restores exact placement. Hard stops: active in-progress encounters on either chart, or conflicting health IDs.
Charts archive instead of deleting: patients.active plus archive_reason, with archivePatient / unarchivePatient flows. Visit corrections record correction_reason rather than rewriting history.

Beyond clinic details, settings carries the backup schedule (backup_schedule, default 13:00), the Drive upload schedule (cloud_backup_schedule), the receipt/invoice consultation fee (consultation_fee, default 0), and the MRN prefix (mrn_prefix, default ND).

Manages the daily patient flow with actionable triage urgency levels. Column Type Description id INTEGER PK Queue entry ID. patient_id INTEGER FK Links to patients.id. status TEXT waiting, in-consult, completed. priority INTEGER Internal priority sort order (1–4). urgency_label TEXT 4-tier urgency: immediate, urgent, priority, routine. triage_notes TEXT Clinical justification for urgency assignment. triaged_by INTEGER FK Links to users.id (Staff member who triaged). triaged_at DATETIME Timestamp of triage assessment. created_at DATETIME Timestamp when patient joined queue. completed_at DATETIME Timestamp when status changed to completed.

Audit log tracking every triage priority reassessment with clinical reason and actor attribution. Column Type Description id INTEGER PK History entry ID. queue_id INTEGER Queue entry ID (preserved as an immutable audit record even after queue removal). previous_priority INTEGER Priority value prior to change. new_priority INTEGER New priority value after reassessment. urgency_label TEXT New urgency label (immediate, urgent, priority, routine). reason TEXT Mandatory clinical justification for reassessment. changed_by INTEGER FK Links to users.id (Staff performing reassessment). changed_at DATETIME Timestamp of change.

Tracks critical system actions for security and compliance. Column Type Description id INTEGER PK Unique Log ID. action TEXT INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. table_name TEXT Target table (e.g., patient_queue). user_id INTEGER ID of the user who performed the action. timestamp DATETIME Time of action (Default: Current Time). details TEXT Description of the change.
This guide describes how to set up the NalamDesk development environment.
Node.js: Version 22.5 or higher (engines in desktop/package.json). npm: Included with Node.js. Git: For version control.

Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/sankara-sabapathy/nalamdesk.git cd nalamdesk Install dependencies: npm install Install Application Dependencies: The application uses Electron, Angular, and native modules (better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers, argon2). The UI stack is Angular 17 with TailwindCSS and daisyUI. Windows: Requires Visual Studio Build Tools (Desktop development with C++) and Python 3. macOS: Requires Xcode Command Line Tools (xcode-select --install) and Python 3. Linux: Requires build-essential and Python 3. npm install inside desktop/ triggers electron-builder install-app-deps (postinstall) to recompile native modules for Electron. npm run postinstall can be run manually if automatic scripts are disabled. npm run postinstall

Default ports are defined in the repo-root .env.development. Override locally with .env.local (gitignored). Port Service 3000 Installed desktop local API (production Electron app) 3001 Cloud API (cloud/api) — cloud/web and desktop cloud sync 3002 Desktop dev local API (cd desktop && npm start) 4200 Desktop Angular dev server Dev and installed apps use separate data directories (NalamDesk-Dev vs NalamDesk) and can run alongside each other.

To start the desktop application in development mode: cd desktop npm start This command will: Start the Angular development server. Compile the Electron main process. Launch the Electron application window.

To build the application for your OS: Windows: npm run dist:win Linux: npm run dist:linux — clinic artifact is the .deb in desktop/release/ (sudo apt install ./nalamdesk-desktop_*_amd64.deb). The AppImage is secondary and requires FUSE 2; do not extract it. Mac: npm run dist:mac Packaged Settings version comes from app:getVersion (app.getVersion() plus optional embedded commit). Feature CI fails the job if artifact names, latest*.yml, build-identity.json, and the displayed version disagree.
NalamDesk tests the desktop app in three layers: unit suites split by process boundary, plus Playwright end-to-end against a throwaway database. Spec files live next to their source (*.spec.ts).

desktop/vitest.workspace.js defines two projects sharing vitest.config.js: Project Files Environment Run renderer src/renderer/**/*.spec.ts jsdom npm run test:renderer (config vitest.config.renderer.mjs) main src/main/**, src/shared/**, src/server/** node npm run test:main (config vitest.config.main.js) npm test runs both. A vitest.config.pure.mjs covers dependency-free modules.

Angular components are tested by manual instantiation with mocked dependencies, not TestBed, to avoid zone.js/ProxyZone instability in JSDOM: // GOOD: Stable & Fast beforeEach(() => { mockService = { getData: vi.fn() }; component = new MyComponent(mockService); }); Template rendering, bindings, and user interactions are verified one layer up, in E2E.

Schema changes ship with assertions in src/main/schema/migrations.spec.ts (each migration v1–v39 applies cleanly and newer grants hold). The shared RBAC model has a conformance spec at src/server/access-conformance.spec.ts. Touching either area means extending its spec first.

desktop/playwright.config.ts (testDir: ./e2e, run with npm run e2e) drives the packaged main process plus renderer: e2e/full-flow.spec.ts: registration → queue → consult → print. e2e/visual.spec.ts, e2e/availability.spec.ts: rendering and presence checks. E2E runs against a transient test database (nalamdesk-test.db, selected when NODE_ENV=test), never the clinic vault: # 1. Close all NalamDesk instances # 2. Build the main process npm run build:main # 3. Run Playwright npm run e2e

Feature CI builds Angular, runs npm test, and (on master pushes) packages all three OS targets. It fails the job when artifact names, latest*.yml, build-identity.json, and the Settings-displayed version disagree — so bump versions and identities together.

For a self-hosted desktop application like NalamDesk, "Enterprise Standard" means Object Storage (S3-compatible). This is the industry standard for secure, scalable, and programmable backups. Unlike Google Drive (which is a personal file host), these services are designed for application data, offering strict compliance (HIPAA/GDPR), encryption, and durability.

Provider Best For Approx Cost Enterprise Features AWS S3 The Gold Standard $0.023/GB 99.999999999% durability, massive compliance certifications (HIPAA, HITECH), region locking (e.g., keep data in Mumbai ap-south-1). Backblaze B2 Cost Efficiency $0.006/GB S3-compatible, extremely cheap, free egress (download) up to 3x, enterprise-grade security. Azure Blob Microsoft Shops Similar to AWS Great if you already use the Microsoft ecosystem. Cloudflare R2 Zero Egress Fees $0.015/GB S3-compatible, no cost to download backups, edge-distributed.

Standard Protocol: If we build an "S3 Connector" for NalamDesk, it works with all of the above (AWS, B2, R2, MinIO). Security: You can create a specific "Bucket" with strict policies (e.g., "Append Only" for ransomware protection). No Vendor Lock-in: You can switch from AWS to Backblaze just by changing the endpoint URL in Settings.

For NalamDesk Enterprise, implementing an S3-Compatible Backup option is the best path forward. It allows users to choose their preferred provider (AWS for strict compliance, Backblaze for cost) while we maintain a single integration codebase.
For self-hosted installations of NalamDesk, you need to configure your own Google Cloud Project to enable Google Drive backups. This ensures you have full control over your data and API usage quotas.

Google requires an OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret to authorize third-party applications (like NalamDesk) to access your Google Drive. Since NalamDesk is open-source, these secrets cannot be embedded in the application code securely. You are the owner of the application instance.
A Google Account (Gmail or Workspace). Access to the Google Cloud Console.
Go to the Google Cloud Console. Click the project dropdown in the top bar and select New Project. Name it NalamDesk-Backup (or similar). Click Create.
In the sidebar, go to APIs & Services > Library. Search for Google Drive API. Click on it and select Enable.

Go to APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen. Select External (for personal @gmail.com accounts) and click Create. Note: In "External" mode, the app will be in "Testing" status. You must add your own email as a Test User. App Information: App name: NalamDesk Backup User support email: Your email. Developer contact information: Your email. Click Save and Continue until you reach Test Users. Test Users: Click + Add Users and enter your google email address. This authorizes you to use your own app. Click Save and Continue.
Go to APIs & Services > Credentials. Click + Create Credentials and select OAuth client ID. Application type: Select Desktop app. Name: Desktop Client. Click Create.

You will see a dialog with your Client ID and Client Secret. Copy these strings. Open NalamDesk Settings > Data & Backup. Enter the Client ID and Client Secret in the respective fields. Click Connect Drive. Security Note: Your Client Secret is stored locally in your encrypted nalamdesk.db database. Never share these credentials.

Settings is admin-only: the route itself refuses non-admin users, so everything below requires an Administrator login. Tabs: General, Users, Security, Data & Backup, Audit Logs, Catalogs, ABDM. The footer shows the packaged version (NalamDesk v0.0.11 (abc1234) style, (development) for dev builds); quote it when reporting defects. Logout clears the session.

Clinic Name: appears on prescriptions, receipts, and reports. Consultation Fee: auto-added as the first invoice line on every visit bill. Zero disables it. Updates: installed version plus Check for updates. Packaged apps check an approved feed; a failed check shows a plain error and never touches the vault. Unsigned or checksum-only feeds do not claim full signature verification.

Click Add User. Fill in: Username (unique, minimum 3 characters, locked after creation), Full Name, Role, mobile (10 digits), email, address, date of birth, joining date, designation. Doctors may carry an HPR ID (optional, preserved across edits). Set a Temporary Password (minimum 6 characters, new users only). Existing users reset through a dedicated workflow, not by editing. Click Save. Built-in roles are admin, doctor, nurse, receptionist. Admins can also compose custom roles from permission templates (Front Desk, Observer, Triage Nurse, Blank) and grant or forbid individual permissions per user with a recorded reason. Some duties stay role-gated no matter what: only doctors finalize encounters, and only doctors and admins merge charts.
Edit: update details or disable the account. Deactivate: batch-disable selected users. Removing a user who owns clinical history is blocked; history is deactivated, never silently deleted.

Change Login Password: changes only the sign-in credential. Rotate Device Envelope: re-protects the unchanged database key for this device. Login passwords and the recovery code are unaffected. Portable Vault Recovery Code: generate the code that restores backups. The previous code stays valid until you confirm the new one — finish the ceremony, don't abandon it halfway.

Diagnosis and medicine inventories plus condition-to-medicine presets. Soft-retire hides a term from typeahead; past visit text is unchanged. Presets fill suggested prescription lines when their condition is diagnosed.

One-time facility setup: HIP ID, counter ID, HFR facility ID, and each doctor's HPR ID. Until credentials are configured the gateway stays in mock mode and everything works offline: the counter QR, scan check-in, callback inbox, and consent-based outside records are documented in the desktop User Guide. Connection test and the pending-callback acknowledgement live on this tab.
A paged grid (50 per page) of security-relevant actions: who did what, to which record, and when. Triage reassessments, merges, overrides, and restores all leave entries here.
Local backups, restore, and Google Drive live under Settings > Data & Backup. See Data & Backups for the full guide.
Daily workflows for receptionists, nurses, and doctors: registration, queue and triage, vitals, and consultations. Everything below works offline.

Navigate to Patients. Click Add Patient. Enter details. Required: Name (at least 3 characters), Mobile (10 digits), Age (0–110), Gender (Male, Female, Other, Unknown). Optional, under collapsed sections: blood group, email, street address, city, state, 6-digit PIN code, emergency contact, and insurance details. Date of birth: pick a date and age fills in automatically, or type the age directly and mark DOB as estimated. Every patient gets an MRN (medical record number, ND-000001 style) automatically. Use it to identify charts precisely. The form warns about Possible existing records (matched by MRN, name + birth date, name, or phone) without blocking you. Click Open on a candidate to check its chart before saving a duplicate. Choose how to finish: Save only: registers the chart and stays on the list. Save & Add to Queue: registers and walks the patient into today's queue at Routine priority in one step. If a duplicate slips through, merge the charts later instead of deleting one. See Merging Duplicate Charts. Every chart carries an auto-assigned MRN. The list shows queue state with Edit and Archive actions.

The Queue orders patients by clinical urgency first, then check-in time. The dashboard can start the next consultation in that order. The queue orders by clinical urgency with triage badges, vitals alerts, and Start Consult actions.

Tier UI label Badge Immediate (priority 4) Immediate (Red) Red, pulsing Urgent (priority 3) Urgent (Orange) Amber Priority (priority 2) Priority (Yellow) Blue Routine (priority 1) Routine (Green) Gray New registrations enter at Routine unless triaged otherwise.
Each row offers Start / Resume Consult plus a menu with Triage reassessment, Record vitals, and Remove from queue. Nurses see no Remove action. Removing asks for a reason (optional).

If a waiting patient's condition changes: Open Triage reassessment on the queue entry. Select the revised urgency level. Enter the mandatory clinical reason. The Update button stays disabled until you do. Confirm. The change lands in the permanent triage history with the previous tier, new tier, reason, and your name.

Record vitals for any patient from the queue row or inside the consultation. The form needs at least one measurement: Blood Pressure: systolic and diastolic together; systolic must be strictly greater than diastolic. Pulse: 30–250 bpm. SpO2: 50–100 %. Respiratory rate: 8–60 per minute. Height: 20–300 cm. Temperature: toggle °F (50–115) / °C (10–46.2). Weight: toggle kg (0.5–500) / lbs (1.1–1100). Switching units converts the typed value; the record keeps what you entered plus the standard unit code. BMI calculates automatically from height and weight. Effective time: when the measurement was taken (defaults to now). Amendments: correcting saved vitals creates a new version linked to the old one with your amendment reason. History is never edited in place. Readings outside clinical thresholds raise a red Abnormal Vitals badge on the queue row, with the details behind it.

Doctors and admins open consults; an admin acts as scribe and must pick the responsible doctor. Only a doctor account finalizes encounters. Go to Queue or Dashboard and open a Waiting or In-Consult patient. Safety banner, SOAP notes, prescription pad with defaults, fee field, and finish actions. 2. Patient Safety Context Banner: allergy count, active problems, and current medications across the top. A green No Known Allergies badge when clear, a red alert with a High Risk flag for life-threatening allergies. 3. Vitals pill: latest BP, pulse, temperature, SpO2, with an Amended tag when corrected. Record or edit from here. 4. Subjective / Objective / Assessment / Plan: symptoms, examination notes, diagnosis (required, Provisional or Final, picked from the clinic condition catalog with Add-new), then the prescription. 5. Prescription pad: medicine typeahead from the clinic catalog, form (Tab, Cap, Syrup, Injection, Ointment, Drop), dose, route (Oral, IV, IM, SC, Topical), frequency (1-0-1, 1-1-1, SOS, STAT…), duration, and instruction (After/Before Food…). Frequency accepts Indian shorthand and Latin SIG interchangeably (BID saves as 1-0-1); unrecognized text is kept verbatim, never dropped. Picking a diagnosis with a configured preset fills suggested lines you can edit first. 6. Allergy Conflict Interceptor: a prescribed drug matching an active allergy stops the save with the substance, criticality, and reaction on screen. Change the drug, or type an explicit clinical override reason to proceed. The reason is stored on the visit. 7. Total Fee (₹): consultation charge for this visit. 8. Footer actions: Save Progress (stay and continue later), Finish & Exit, Finish & Next (close and open the next waiting patient), Postpone, Print, and Download PDF in view mode. Copy to Current pulls a previous visit's content forward for editing. 9. Prescription QR: printed PDFs carry a scannable QR in the footer encoding the medicines, doses, routes, schedules, patient, doctor, and date (compressed, versioned ND1. payload). Any scanner reading the code recovers the structured prescription offline. Oversized prescriptions print without a QR rather than an unscannable one. The QR is a convenience copy: always cross-check against the printed prescription and the doctor's signature. 9. Complete Consultation: signing stamps the responsible doctor's name, license number, and specialty onto the visit, marks it finished, and syncs prescribed medicines into the active medication list. Only a finished encounter can be billed (see Daily Collection).

The Daily Collection card on the Dashboard shows today's money position at a glance. It is visible to Admins, Doctors, and Receptionists. Every figure is derived live from the payment ledger, never from stored totals, so the numbers always reconcile.

Collected today: net amount collected for the clinic-local day (payments minus reversals), in ₹. To review: count of payments that need attention. Zero means clean. Subtitle reads Today's receipts and reconciliation before the first payment lands. Click the card to open the Daily close modal. The dashboard surfaces the queue, visits, and the Daily Collection card.

Header shows the date and the note Derived from payment transactions, not stored totals. Collected: the net total for the day. By method: one row per payment method and kind, with transaction count. Reversal rows subtract from the net. Invoices created: invoices raised today grouped by status, with count and total. Needs review: payments that need a human look. A payment lands here when it is a reversal, or when it is a non-cash payment with no reference recorded. Each row shows the receipt number, kind, amount, method, the invoice it belongs to, and the recorded reason if any. Non-cash rows missing a reference are flagged missing ref. When nothing needs attention, the section reads Clean, nothing to review.

Billing lives inside the consultation workbench, next to the Total Fee field, and is visible to admins, doctors, and receptionists. Create invoice: allowed only after the encounter is finished. The invoice starts with the clinic's configured consultation fee (when non-zero) plus the visit's charge lines. Totals are computed from the lines; every invoice gets a unique number. Record payment: cash, UPI, or card. Amounts must be positive and cannot exceed the balance. Each payment is idempotent and gets a unique receipt number. Receipt: open and print any payment's receipt. Reprints carry a DUPLICATE watermark; Print last receipt reprints the latest. Refund: reverses a payment in whole or part with a mandatory reason. Refunds appear as reversal rows and land in the day-close review queue. Over-refunds are refused. Void: cancels an invoice with a mandatory reason. Invoices with outstanding payments cannot be voided. Invoices are never edited or deleted. Corrections flow through refunds and voids with reasons, so the ledger always reconciles. The day-close modal verifies exactly that.

An invoice is raised per visit after the encounter is finished. The app refuses to bill an in-progress visit. The invoice starts with the clinic's configured consultation fee (which may be zero) plus the visit's charge lines. Totals are computed from the lines; they are never typed in. Invoices are immutable. Corrections go through reversals with a recorded reason, which then appear in the review queue. Nothing is silently edited or deleted. Days follow the clinic-local timezone, so a payment near midnight counts toward the right clinic day.

When you launch NalamDesk for the first time, you will be greeted by the Setup Wizard. This process initializes your local secure database (the "Vault") where all patient data is stored encrypted. On Linux, install the .deb clinic package (sudo apt install ./nalamdesk-desktop_*_amd64.deb). First-run encryption uses the system keyring (gnome-libsecret). If setup reports ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE, install libsecret-1-0 and gnome-keyring and restart — do not use --password-store=basic.
You will see a "Welcome to NalamDesk" screen. Click "Get Started" to begin.

Enter the details for your practice. These details will appear on: Prescription headers. Bills and Invoices. Patient communications. Required Fields: Clinic Name: (e.g., "City Health Clinic") Doctor Name: (e.g., "Dr. Smith") Specialization: (e.g., "General Physician")

Create the primary Administrator account. This account has full access to all settings. Fields: Username: Choose a unique username (e.g., admin). Password: Must be at least 4 characters long. Confirm Password: Re-enter to verify. Important: If you lose this password, you cannot recover the encrypted data easily without the Recovery Key.
The system will generate a Recovery Key. SAVE THIS KEY: Write it down or save it in a password manager. This key is the only way to reset your password if you forget it.
Once verified, you will be redirected to the Login Screen. Enter your new credentials to access the Dashboard. Sign in with your username and password. Logout clears the session.
If you see this message, a database already exists on this machine. Solution: logging in with existing credentials. Use the "Forgot Password" flow if needed.
Welcome to the NalamDesk User Guide. This section is designed to help Doctors, Receptionists, and Administrators effectively use the application.

Install: Windows .exe, macOS .dmg, or Linux .deb (sudo apt install ./nalamdesk-desktop_*_amd64.deb). The AppImage is secondary and needs FUSE 2; do not extract it. Initial Setup: Step-by-step guide to initializing your secure Vault. Admin Management: Learn how to set up the clinic, manage users, and configure backups. Clinic Operations: A guide to daily workflows like patient registration, queue management, and consultations. Daily Collection: Receipts, the review queue, and the ledger-derived day close. Merging Duplicate Charts: Preview-first merge with rollback for duplicate patient records. Data & Backups: Local backup schedule, retention, restore, and Google Drive redundancy.

Role Key Responsibilities Admin System configuration, User creation, Custom roles, Data backups. Doctor Consulting patients, Creating prescriptions, Viewing history, Merging duplicate charts. Receptionist Registering patients, Managing the waiting queue, Recording payments, Archiving charts. Nurse Recording vitals, Monitoring the triage queue. Only doctors finalize encounters; only doctors and admins merge charts or edit safety data. Admins can compose custom roles, but clinical finalization and merges stay gated regardless.

When the same person ends up with two charts (a walk-in registered twice, a name spelled two ways), merge them instead of deleting one. Merging moves the full history onto one surviving chart through a preview with a mandatory audited reason, and it is reversible. Only Doctors and Admins can merge. The chart header offers Merge (doctors and admins) next to Start Consultation.

During New Patient Registration, the form warns about possible existing records (matched by name, mobile, or MRN) without blocking you. Click a candidate to open its chart before deciding. The warning never stops a registration: a queue that cannot add a walk-in patient is worse than a duplicate.

Open the chart you are working from and click Merge. Search for the other chart by name, mobile, or MRN (at least 2 characters). Candidates show how they matched. Pick the survivor: Keep this chart or Keep the other chart. The preview shows exactly what moves: per-record counts of what the absorbed chart holds. Read the red warnings if any appear: A chart with an active in-progress encounter cannot merge. Finish the encounter first. This applies to both charts. Two charts holding different health IDs cannot merge. Unlink one first. Enter the reason (required, written to the audit trail). Confirm Merge charts. The dialog states what happens: history moves to the surviving chart, the absorbed chart stays reachable, and the merge is reversible.

A merged-away chart shows an Unmerge button. Confirming moves its history back and clears the merge link. The merge itself stays in the audit trail permanently: unmerging reverses the data, never the record that it happened.

Archiving is for charts that should leave the active list without losing history (moved away, deceased, entered in error and replaced). Admins, doctors, and receptionists can archive a chart with a recorded reason; unarchiving restores it. Archive when the chart itself is unwanted; merge when two charts describe the same person.

Closed Source vs. Open Source: WhatsApp is a proprietary, closed-source application. They embed their Client ID and Secret deep inside their compiled application code (APK/IPA). Because the source code is not public, it is "harder" (though not impossible) for attackers to extract these secrets. NalamDesk is open-source. If we committed our Client Secret to GitHub, anyone could see it and use it to impersonate our app, leading to Google banning our API access immediately. Verified Publisher Trust: Meta (Facebook) is a verified publisher with Google. They assume liability for how their embedded secret is used. As an open-source project, we cannot assume liability for every self-hosted instance.
documents.s: Why WhatsApp doesn't ask for Client ID/Secret?

documents.t: Tools like rclone, Duplicati, and others that integrate with Google Drive often follow this "Bring Your Own Key" model for the same security reasons. It gives you (the user) complete control and ensures your data isn't dependent on a developer's API quota or standing.
